text:
Pavel Buchnevich has one point in his last ten games and none in his last six, and on a St. Louis team trying to find its footing, that's a problem. He has seven points in 19 games after 48 last season.

Our read is that he's due rather than done. Over those ten games the Blues have actually had a bit more than his usual rate of chances with him on the ice, 10.5 expected goals (the quality of chances) against 9.9, and the pucks just haven't gone in. For the season he has 3 goals on 4.9 expected, and St. Louis takes 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, almost 7 points better than without him. That's a player helping his team win the ice. The Hockey Writers even named him among the Blues' standouts of a recent week.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has a signature for him: 19% of his setups come from behind the net, more than twice a typical forward's rate. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, though, which tempers the enthusiasm. Our talent range has him near 40 points. If the finishing turns, his numbers will move quickly.
